comparator.route: Economics of Markets and Organisations major
comparator.sourceNotes: The current programme is a 180-EC three-year bachelor with a broad 60-EC first year and 60-EC second year in economics, business economics and quantitative methods, followed by 60 EC of third-year choice, Career Skills, a formal major and an individual thesis. The public curriculum and current programme-family overview establish the first- and second-year subjects, 24 EC of first-half third-year choice space, Career Skills, and a major consisting of one seminar plus three major courses. This pathway instantiates Economics of Markets and Organisations as the broadest continuation of the generic programme's emphasis on markets, firms and organisational choices; the route is selected independently of UCR fit.

alternatives.label: Economics, business & data
alternatives.labelReason: The completed UCR curriculum is broader than pure economics: it combines micro- and macroeconomics with accounting, finance, marketing, strategy, organisational study, data science, econometrics and international business.
alternatives.concept: A broad closest feasible response to Economics and Business Economics combining markets, macroeconomics and policy with accounting, finance, marketing, strategy, organisations, statistics, data and econometrics.
progression: Business, economics, data, research, mathematical and strategic foundations precede the advanced policy, organisational, international-business, machine-learning, econometrics, behavioural-economics, market-research and finance work. Strategy follows Business Foundations; Probability & Statistics follows Mathematical Methods; Money, Banking & Finance follows business, accounting and economic study. All formal prerequisites occur earlier and all courses are offered in their assigned terms.
traceOverrides: provides multivariate statistics and experimental methods that strengthen empirical economic and business research

alternatives.label: Behavioural economics, marketing & consumer decisions
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines behavioural economics with social psychology, experimental methods, marketing, persuasion, product design and data analysis, so the label reflects both the behavioural foundation and its consumer/marketing application.
alternatives.concept: A behavioural-economics and consumer-decision route combining economic choice with psychology, experiments, marketing, persuasion, product design and empirical analysis.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad closest match, this route replaces Mathematical Methods, Probability & Statistics, the AI-economy course, international business and finance with social psychology, rhetoric, leadership communication, persuasive communication and negotiation. The resulting curriculum retains the common economics, business and empirical core but makes human influence, consumer response and strategic communication a distinct organising emphasis.
progression: Foundational economics, business, rhetoric, social psychology and research methods precede advanced microeconomics, public economics, marketing, organisational psychology, persuasive communication, behavioural economics, econometrics and market research. The introductory rhetoric course precedes Persuasive Communication, and Microeconomics & Behavior precedes Behavioral Economics. All formal prerequisites occur earlier and all courses are offered in their assigned terms.

alternatives.label: Finance, economics & quantitative analysis
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is organised around finance and economics with substantial mathematics, programming, data, econometrics and optimisation, rather than implying a specialist finance degree without a quantitative core.
alternatives.concept: A financial-economics route combining money, banking and corporate finance with micro- and macroeconomics, public economics, econometrics, probability, calculus, programming, databases, machine learning and optimisation.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad closest match, this route replaces experimental methods, marketing, consumer-product work, organisational psychology and market research with programming, database systems, computational decision-making, linear algebra and advanced calculus. It therefore retains the economics and business core while making quantitative financial and economic analysis the organising emphasis. It differs still more clearly from the behavioural route, which concentrates on psychology, marketing, persuasion and consumer response.
progression: Business Foundations precedes Strategy & Digital Transformation and Money, Banking & Finance. Mathematical Methods precedes Probability & Statistics, Linear Algebra and Advanced Calculus; programming precedes computational decision-making; accounting, economics, data and research foundations precede the final finance, econometrics and behavioural-economics work. All formal prerequisites occur earlier and all courses are offered in their assigned terms.

routeSelection.route: Economics of Markets and Organisations major
routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is the generic Economics and Business Economics bachelor. The current programme family offers several formal third-year majors. Economics of Markets and Organisations most broadly continues the common curriculum's study of markets, firms, incentives and organisational choices rather than selecting a narrower application such as finance or marketing. The choice is independent of UCR fit.

selection.assessment: The broad closest match covers the programme-wide generator interests. The two remaining coherent generator-backed directions are behavioural economics with consumer/marketing decision-making and financial economics/financial markets. Both yield feasible curricula that are substantively distinct from the closest match and from each other, so the maximum of three UCR alternatives is reached.

blocks: Public Economics overlaps with fiscal economics through taxation, public intervention and distribution, but is broader than the comparator course.
The comparator contains a dedicated History of Economic Thought course. UCR does not add an unrelated history course merely to imitate this component.
Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations overlaps with organisation, markets and strategy but does not reproduce the comparator course in full.
Market Research provides applied research design, data collection and analysis for business questions, but is not the same as the comparator-wide research project.
International Business & Governance overlaps with international economic and institutional environments but is broader and more business-governance oriented.
Research Methods & Statistics provides statistics and empirical research foundations, but is broader than Applied Statistics 1.
Linear Algebra directly covers matrix and vector methods in the comparator course, but not its full calculus, game-theory and linear-programming combination.
Personal & Professional Development overlaps with academic and professional formation but does not reproduce the comparator's economics-specific Academic Skills modules.

notes.text: Erasmus Economics and Business Economics provides a fixed two-year sequence including dedicated History of Economic Thought, intermediate accounting and deeper programme-specific economics/statistics, followed by a formal third-year major, seminar and thesis. UCR can build coherent economics/business, behavioural-consumer and finance/quantitative programmes, but it does not reproduce that full specialist sequence. In particular, no unrelated history course is added merely to imitate the comparator's History of Economic Thought component.
